mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT has climbed from -38.4 to -13.1 over three weeks, an almost monotone return of station footfall that proxies the reconstruction of pre-pandemic trip chains; because discretionary retail trips are typically chained onto transit legs, continued transit convergence mechanically pulls RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT weekly mean rose +25.3 points between t-3w and t-0w
fact:RETAIL_REC weekly mean rose +23.2 points over the same span
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than its last-28-day mean of -13.5 in the majority of weeks where TRANSIT continues to close on baseline.

mechanism_narrative: The joint recovery of WORKPLACES (-41.7 to -19.7) and TRANSIT (-38.4 to -13.1) is a commuting-normalization composite: office return restores weekday lunchtime, after-work and errand traffic that retail-and-recreation venues depend on. The two series reinforce each other, so the interaction term, not either alone, drives the up-move in RETAIL_REC.
evidence_refs: fact:both series improved in each of the last three weeks
failure_condition: When WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improve week-on-week, RETAIL_REC over the following 28 days still fails to exceed its prior-28-day mean in more than half of observed weeks.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL has decayed from +4.7 to +1.4, meaning households are spending progressively less time at home. Once the residential stay-at-home premium drops below roughly +1.5 points, home-based substitution for shopping and leisure has effectively unwound, releasing visits into retail-and-recreation venues within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean falls below +1.5 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 4.7 to 1.4 across t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL drops below +1.5 yet RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days averages at or below its trailing 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has crossed into positive territory (+11.3) while TRANSIT recovery decelerates from +8.7 to +7.9 points per week; the combination marks precautionary household behaviour re-asserting itself. When routine-goods traffic rises faster than transit reopening, discretionary retail demand is being substituted away, capping RETAIL_REC below its current level within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM weekly mean crosses above +8 percent while TRANSIT week-on-week gain falls below +8 points
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM turned positive at t-2w and reached +11.3 at t-0w
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM stays above +8 while TRANSIT gains slow, but RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days still exceeds its trailing 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS peaked at 72.1 and has already slipped to 68.3, the classic late-summer outdoor-activity rollover. Because park visits and discretionary retail compete for the same weekend hours, the decline in outdoor engagement combined with the fading residential premium moves spending indoors into retail-and-recreation over the following four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean falls more than 3 points below its 4-week maximum
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell 3.8 points between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: PARKS continues falling below its 4-week maximum while RESIDENTIAL stays under +2, yet RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days averages below its trailing 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: The monotone four-week rise in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT is only consistent with administrative capacity limits being relaxed in stages rather than a purely voluntary return. Under an easing-restrictions regime, each policy step raises the legal ceiling on retail occupancy, so RETAIL_REC converges upward toward baseline over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:no week-on-week deterioration in either series across t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days lands below -13.5 despite TRANSIT and WORKPLACES continuing to improve week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are the fastest-moving policy-sensitive series; if either registers a week-on-week reversal while RESIDENTIAL ticks back up, that combination signals re-imposed restrictions or a formal advisory, which would drag RETAIL_REC down over the following four weeks by removing legal and perceived trip capacity.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT or WORKPLACES falls more than 5 points week-on-week while RESIDENTIAL rises more than 1 point week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL moved opposite to TRANSIT and WORKPLACES in every reported week
regime_hint: tightening restrictions or formal health advisory
failure_condition: TRANSIT or WORKPLACES drops over 5 points week-on-week with RESIDENTIAL up over 1 point, yet RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days still exceeds its trailing 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM turning positive (+11.3) shows in-person routine shopping trips have been fully restored; these trips are habit-forming and spatially co-located with retail-and-recreation strips, so restored routine shopping immediately lifts adjacent discretionary visits. The effect is fast-acting and should register within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose 20.3 points from -9.0 to +11.3 while RETAIL_REC rose 23.2 points
failure_condition: In the week following a GROCERY_PHARM reading above +10, RETAIL_REC fails to post a higher weekly mean than the week before.
